summary.title: Exercism
summary.one_liner: Exercism is a free, community-funded platform for learning programming in 85 languages through coding exercises, automated feedback, and mentoring.
takeaways: Exercism offers coding exercises across 85 programming languages at no cost.
The main workflow is CLI-first: download and submit exercises from the terminal.
An in-browser editor lets you try a language without installing it locally.
Automatic analysis gives quick feedback and improvement points on solutions.
Human mentors review code to point out knowledge gaps and idiomatic conventions.
summary.summary: The Exercism homepage describes a practice platform with coding exercises (such as Allergies, Zebra Puzzle and queen attack problems) in 85 programming languages. It is presented as free and run by a community-funded, not-for-profit organisation. Solutions can be submitted via a CLI tool or an in-browser editor, receive automated analysis, and can be reviewed by mentors who help learners write idiomatic code. The page also points beginners to a separate platform called Jiki.
